## Positioning

Lorenz builds cost-resilient, deterministic, self-hosted automation that beats the AI "token tax."

The core argument: autonomous AI agents can burn 5-30x the tokens of a single chatbot call (Gartner). LLM API prices are currently subsidized below true compute cost — Sequoia framed this as the "$600B question." Repricing has already started, with some premium models priced at 3.6-6x base rate. When the subsidy ends, the bill lands on the business, not the vendor. His job: make sure it never does.

His method:
1. "Can a rule decide this?" YES -> deterministic logic (cost $0, hallucinations 0).
2. NO -> capped model call (semantic-cached, cheapest-capable-model routed).
3. Human-in-the-loop gate on anything touching money or client records.
4. Every build ships with validation, retries, fallback paths, PII-masked audit logging, and docs from day one.

Taglines:
- "I build automation that runs on logic, not your AI budget."
- "AI on a leash, used surgically, only where it earns its cost."

## Services (detailed)

### Automation & Cost Audit — from ~$750
Map all current workflows, identify the highest-ROI automation candidates, and surface redundant SaaS spend. Deliverable: prioritized automation roadmap with ROI estimates and a list of tool consolidation opportunities. Engagement is fixed-scope and time-boxed.

### Build & Ship — from $2,500
Fixed-scope automation built end-to-end: trigger, validate, process, integrate, audit log. Includes error handling with retry/fallback paths, PII-masked logging, and documentation. Typically delivered within 2-4 weeks. No open-ended retainers, no scope creep.

### AI Agents & Orchestration
Production agents wired to real tools, gated by human approval, built with evals and guardrails. Agents follow the deterministic-first method: rule-based where possible, model-based where necessary, always with a human-in-the-loop gate on business-critical actions.

### Fractional Automation Engineering — retainer from $1,500/month
Ongoing ownership of the automation backlog. Lorenz operates as an embedded automation engineer: triages new requests, maintains existing workflows, adds monitoring, and incrementally improves the stack. Suited to ops-heavy teams that want continuous automation capacity without a full-time hire.

## Case studies (anonymized)

### Case study 1: Lead intake pipeline (-70% manual data entry)
A law firm's lead intake required staff to manually re-key data between three systems: the web form, the CRM, and the case management platform. The process took 15-20 minutes per lead and introduced frequent data errors.

Lorenz replaced it with an n8n webhook pipeline: form submission triggers validation, deduplication, and automated record creation across all three systems in under 10 seconds. A single capped AI call handles unstructured field normalization; everything else is deterministic.

**Result:** -70% manual data entry on the 3-system pipeline. Zero leads lost between systems. Token spend held to one capped call per lead.

### Case study 2: Lead scoring and conversion (+30% conversion)
A service business was manually reviewing and routing inbound leads, with no consistent scoring. High-value leads were being routed at the same priority as tire-kickers, and follow-up timing was inconsistent.

Lorenz built an n8n + hybrid AI pipeline: a rule-based pre-filter scores leads on deterministic signals (source, form completeness, service requested), then a single capped AI call enriches ambiguous cases. Priority leads go to an immediate personal follow-up queue; lower-priority leads to a nurture sequence.

**Result:** +30% lead conversion on a capped AI budget, with no open-ended AI bill.

### Case study 3: Billing sync (zero missed invoices)
A professional services firm was running billing reconciliation manually: pulling records from a case management system (Filevine/Clio) and matching them against invoices in the billing platform. Missed invoices and late charges were a recurring problem.

Lorenz built a deterministic n8n sync: nightly schedule triggers a read from the case management API, compares against the billing system, flags discrepancies, and auto-creates missing invoices. Zero AI in the path — the logic is pure rule-based matching. Discrepancies trigger a human-review alert before any write.

**Result:** Zero missed invoices since go-live. No manual reconciliation. Zero tokens on a business-critical money flow.

## Open source (github.com/lorenzespinosa)

- **openclaw-n8n-stack** — one-command Docker stack: OpenClaw AI agent gateway + n8n + PostgreSQL, MCP pre-wired. For teams that want a private, self-hosted AI agent backend without cloud vendor lock-in.
- **n8n-error-handling-pattern** — production-grade n8n error handling: retry with exponential backoff, dead-letter queue, fallback paths, audit logging. The pattern Lorenz applies on every build.
- **n8n-ai-agent-delegator** — routes plain-language commands to specialist agents, with confidence scoring and human-in-the-loop gates. Multi-agent orchestration without a cloud orchestration bill.
- **airtable-automation-toolkit** — Airtable as a reliable staging layer: dead-letter queue, PII-masked audit logging, bidirectional sync patterns.
- **n8n-legal-ops-templates** — production-tested n8n workflow templates for legal operations: missed-call recovery, billing sync, intake routing, case management updates. Zero real client data.
- **n8n-lint** — CLI linter for n8n workflow JSON. Catches credential leaks, deprecated nodes, and orphaned connections. 16 rules. CI-ready. Run it before shipping any workflow.
- **openclaw-setup-guide** — step-by-step guide to setting up the OpenClaw self-hosted AI stack.
- **openphone-n8n-connector** — production connector between OpenPhone and n8n for missed-call recovery, voicemail transcription, and CRM sync.

## FAQ

**What kinds of businesses do you work with?**
Primarily ops-heavy service businesses: law firms, medical practices, consulting firms, agencies. Any business where manual data entry, missed follow-ups, or tool sprawl are eating into margins.

**Do you work with AI or without?**
Both, and the choice depends on the task. For anything deterministic (data routing, field matching, invoice reconciliation), Lorenz uses pure rule-based logic: faster, cheaper, and zero hallucination risk. For tasks that genuinely require language understanding (unstructured input normalization, intent classification), he adds a single capped model call with human-in-the-loop approval on anything business-critical.

**Why self-hosted n8n instead of Zapier or Make?**
Zapier and Make are per-task-priced, which penalizes high-volume use cases. Self-hosted n8n on a small VPS runs at a flat monthly cost regardless of volume. Your data also stays on infrastructure you own, which matters for client-data-heavy industries like law and healthcare.

**What does an engagement look like?**
It starts with a free 15-minute call to understand the process and the pain. Most engagements follow this sequence: audit (1-2 weeks, scoped) -> build (2-4 weeks per workflow, fixed-scope) -> optionally, a retainer for ongoing ownership. No scope creep, no surprise invoices.

**Do you sign NDAs?**
Yes. All client data and business details stay confidential. The open-source repos contain zero real client data.
